sections.counts:
The log holds up on the big lifts. All five squat sets, deadlift sets 1–3 and bench sets 1–2 and 4–5 agree with what you logged once unrack and set-down cycles are set aside. Bench set 3 shows 7 cycles for 6 logged; the seventh is the slow press back to the rack. Deadlift sets 4 and 5 were found (5 and 3 slow pulls about 5 s apart) but the automatic counter cannot count reps that slow yet, so their counts on this page come from the manual check, not the counter. Three machine and cable counts on this page are the counter's errors, not yours: leg curl set 2 reads 25 because the wrist ripples twice per rep, leg curl set 1 reads 10 through two regrips, and pulldown set 1 reads 4 because the counter stopped at a pause after the fourth pull (8 pulls are visible in the trace).

You wrote that you lost count on the pushdowns: the watch shows 12 and 10 clean forearm swings, exactly what you logged. The hammer curls are the open question: the watch arm made exactly 10 curls in set 1 (12 logged) and 6 in set 2 (7 logged). The same 10-for-12 showed up on 1 Nov, so either the count runs high or some reps are done one arm at a time.
sections.velocity:
Squat speed was steady across the three 105 kg sets: 0.55, 0.52 and 0.53 m/s on average, with the best rep at 0.58–0.60 m/s each time. That matches RPE 7–7.5 staying flat. Bench slowed as expected: 0.29 → 0.26 → 0.26 m/s at 80 kg while RPE climbed 7.5 → 8 → 8.5, and the last rep of the last set took clearly longer than the rest.

Deadlift sets 1–3 moved at 0.45–0.49 m/s regardless of load (60, 90, 110 kg). No velocity is shown for deadlift sets 4–5: the reps were too slow for the height filter to isolate, and a number there would be invented.
sections.load_velocity: No velocity-based 1RM is shown today, on purpose. Squat best-rep speed was 0.76 m/s at 60 kg, 0.59 at 80 kg and 0.58–0.60 at 105 kg: flat from 80 to 105 kg, so the 80 kg warm-up was not pushed hard and the line is not trustworthy (r² 0.72). Bench falls with load (0.55 → 0.41 → about 0.31 m/s at 40 / 60 / 80 kg) but set 3's best rep is inflated by the re-rack cycle (r² 0.64). Deadlift speed did not change with load at all (0.49–0.51 m/s). From load, reps and RPE alone the estimates are about 133 kg squat, 143 kg deadlift and 103 kg bench. Warm-ups moved with full intent would make the velocity lines usable.
sections.classifier: Squat and lying leg curl are new to the system, so nothing learned earlier could name them. Squat is easy to tell apart from now on: it is the only lift with the wrist cocked back beside the shoulder (gravity about +0.75 on x, −0.5 on z). Bench, deadlift, pushdown and hammer curl look the same as on 1 Nov, which is what makes them recognisable across days.
sections.detection: The recording is complete this time (65 minutes, no gaps). Automatic placement put 13 of 23 sets in the right spot. The misses, all corrected by hand: the squats were shifted by one set (warm-up movement was taken for set 1, and the real fifth set was left out), deadlift sets 4–5 and leg curl set 1 were placed on setup movement, and leg curl set 2 and pulldown set 1 were cut in half. Two rhythmic blocks are not in the log and are left unlabelled: about 17 wrist rotations at 35–36 min, between deadlift and bench.
sections.rest: Rests on the main lifts were 3–4.5 minutes for working sets (squat 176–281 s, deadlift 194–238 s, bench 190–244 s). The last deadlift triple came after only 83 s, which fits it stopping at 3 reps. Pushdowns and hammer curls were done with 35–55 s between sets, straight through rather than as a superset.

signature_desc.Squat (Barbell): Wrist cocked back beside the shoulder with the bar on the back: gravity about +0.75 on x. Almost no rotation; a sharp down-up every 4–5 s.
signature_desc.Deadlift (Barbell): Arm hanging straight, gravity on −x. Long reps with a pause at the floor; the heaviest sets ran about 5 s per rep.
signature_desc.Bench Press (Barbell): Forearm vertical, gravity fully on +x. Pure vertical travel of about 37–43 cm, very little rotation.
signature_desc.Lying Leg Curl (Machine): Hands on the handles, arm along −x. The wrist barely moves: a ripple of 7–8 cm per rep is all the watch sees.
signature_desc.Lat Pulldown (Cable): Arm overhead (+x), concentric downwards, about 60 cm of travel per pull.
signature_desc.Triceps Rope Pushdown: Forearm swings from about horizontal to hanging; gravity on x sweeps from +0.4 to −0.95 each rep.
signature_desc.Hammer Curl (Dumbbell): The largest rotation of the session: forearm from hanging to upright, gravity on x flips from −1 to about +0.8.
